import.acknowledge: I understand this cookie set is equivalent to the account password.
import.expiryNotice: This session is expected to expire on {date}. A notification goes out before it does.

risk.equivalence: A logged-in cookie set is equivalent to the account password: whoever holds it can act as that account.
risk.storage: It is stored encrypted and no endpoint ever returns it, but an administrator of this instance can use it.
risk.dedicated: Use an account kept for this purpose, never your main one.

import.maskNote: Values are masked by the server; the console never receives them.
import.usableHint: Whether this cookie set can be used as an identity.

test.title: Identity test
test.businessErrorNote: A business error counts as a pass: the platform answered, the content is simply gone.

settings.readOnly: Your role can read settings but not change them.

source.environmentHint: Read from the environment at startup. It applies because no database override exists.
source.defaultHint: Built-in default. Neither the database nor the environment sets this key.

sensitive.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change a sensitive key.

row.alreadyInherited: Already inherited; there is no override to remove.

confirm.warning: This key widens the attack surface. The URL allowlist is the only SSRF defence this service has, the CORS origins decide which sites may hold your API keys, and the download proxy turns this server into a relay.
confirm.audit: The change is written to the audit log with your account and the previous value.

empty.title: No settings to show

groupHint.sched: Waiting, queueing, cooldowns and the thresholds that trip an endpoint.
groupHint.pool: Water marks and the conservative per-identity request rate.
groupHint.signing: Which signer produces the request signature. The in-process algorithms no longer match what either platform sends, so the browser is the working default.
groupHint.cache: How long a parsed result stays reusable.
groupHint.snapshot: Deduplication window for writes to the content history.
groupHint.retention: How long logs, events and tasks are kept. Content snapshots are never deleted automatically.
groupHint.api: Abuse limits, the long-poll ceiling and the default response language.
groupHint.security: Every key here is sensitive: allowlists, CORS and the download proxy.
groupHint.notify: Delivery switch, channels and the default alert language.
groupHint.system: Instance behaviour, including the opt-in update check.
groupHint.other: Keys with no group of their own.

signing.mode.rpc: Browser (recommended) - runs the platform's own script
signing.mode.auto: In-process, switching to the browser when signatures start failing

security.request_proxy.deny: Refuse it (recommended) - callers cannot choose an egress
security.request_proxy.public: Allow, public addresses only - loopback and private ranges are refused
security.request_proxy.any: Allow anything - an API key holder can reach this server's own network

notifications.dedupExplainer: Every trigger carries a deduplication window: the same alert goes out once per window and is suppressed until it closes. Without that, one open circuit sends a notification per request, and the first thing anyone does is switch alerting off. Alerting is trustworthy because it is rare.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.description: The global switch, and the language used when a channel does not set its own.
delivery.enabledHint: While this is off, triggers still fire and are recorded, but nothing is delivered.
delivery.languageHint: An alert is rendered for whoever receives it, not for the console operator.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Where alerts are delivered. A webhook target must be https and must not resolve to a private address.

triggers.title: Triggers and deduplication windows
triggers.description: The event set is fixed. A channel receives every event unless you narrow it.

empty.title: No channels yet
empty.description: Alerts stay inside the console until a channel exists. Add one so an incident reaches you when nobody is looking at this page.

editor.title: Channel
editor.description: Credentials are stored on the server and are never shown in full again.

field.urlHint: https only. Loopback, private and link-local addresses are refused.
field.groupHint: Groups these notifications together on the device.
field.secretHint: Optional. Set it when the bot is secured by a signature rather than a keyword.
field.languageHint: This channel renders its alerts in this language.
field.eventsHint: Clear what this channel should not receive. The deduplication window of each event is fixed and shown beside it.
field.enabledHint: A disabled channel is kept but skipped.
field.maskedHint: Shown masked. Leave it untouched to keep the stored value; type a new one to replace it, or clear it to remove it.

step.pool: How many identities are usable, and how long since the oldest one succeeded.
step.signing: The local algorithm and the browser produce the same signature.
step.smoke: One fixed public link is fetched end to end.

options.description: All six steps run in order. Each has its own timeout, so a hung dependency cannot stall the rest.
options.smokeHint: Step 6 pulls one fixed public link through the whole pipeline. Turn it off to keep the run entirely local.

backup.keyExplainer: Credentials are exported as ciphertext and the archive never contains the master key. A restore therefore needs the same DTK_SECRET_KEY that created it; under a different key the proxy URLs and cookie jars cannot be decrypted.
backup.adminOnly: Only an administrator can create or restore a backup.
backup.restoreDone: Restored {name}. Reload the console so every page reads the new data.

create.title: Create a backup
create.description: Settings, proxies, content snapshots, users and API keys are always included. Request logs and identity events are not: they describe a run that is over.
create.includeIdentitiesHint: Off by default. An identity is bound to one proxy and one egress address, so it should not be reused after a move.
create.includeIdentitiesWarning: The archive will carry logged-in cookie jars as ciphertext. On another machine the exit address differs, and using these identities from it is exactly what gets them risk-controlled. Restore them only onto the same egress.
create.hint: The archive is written on the server, beside the other backups.

list.title: Archives
list.description: Backups the server can see, newest first.

empty.title: No backups yet
empty.description: Content snapshots accumulate over months and cannot be fetched again once the platform drops them. Create the first archive now.

confirm.title: Restore this archive?
confirm.description: Type the file name to confirm.
confirm.warning: A restore writes the archive over the current database. Rows present in both are replaced by the archived version.
confirm.keyReminder: This instance must hold the same DTK_SECRET_KEY that created the archive.

keyMismatch.title: The master key does not match
keyMismatch.body: This archive was created under a different DTK_SECRET_KEY, so nothing was restored. Going ahead would leave every proxy URL and cookie jar undecryptable, and the server refused rather than half-restoring.
keyMismatch.action: Restore with the original key, or start from a fresh instance and re-import what you can.

users.adminOnly: Only an administrator can manage accounts. Your own password and sessions are below.
users.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete the account you are signed in with.

list.title: Accounts
list.description: A role change takes effect on the next request; there is no cache to wait for.

empty.title: No accounts
empty.description: Every instance has at least one administrator.

matrix.title: What each role can do
matrix.description: Three roles, no groups and no per-object permissions: a self-hosted instance has a handful of users, and a rule set that fits on one screen is one people actually follow.

capability.read: Read the overview, logs and diagnostics
capability.sensitive: Change sensitive settings: allowlist, CORS, download proxy

password.title: Your password
password.description: Changing it signs out every other device, because the usual reason to change a password is that it may have leaked.
password.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
password.changedHint: Other devices have been signed out.

sessions.title: Your sessions
sessions.description: One row per signed-in device. A session is identified by a digest of its token, never by the token itself.
sessions.signOutFailed: Could not sign the other devices out
sessions.emptyDescription: This is the only signed-in device.

create.title: Add a user
create.description: Give the smallest role that lets the person do their work; it can be raised later.
create.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore. Three characters or more.
create.roleHint: The capability matrix above explains each role.

confirm.deleteWarning: The account and every session it opened are removed. The last administrator cannot be deleted.
confirm.signOutDescription: Every session except this one is revoked immediately.

apiKeys.createDescription: The full key is shown once, right after it is created. Store it before closing the dialog.
apiKeys.createdDescription: Copy it now. The server keeps only the prefix and a hash of the secret.
apiKeys.createdWarning: Nobody, administrators included, can read this value again. If it is lost, revoke the key and create another one.
apiKeys.createdAck: I have stored this key somewhere safe
apiKeys.activeCount: {count, plural, one {# active key} other {# active keys}}
apiKeys.nameHint: Something recognisable in the audit log, such as the script or host that will use it.
apiKeys.scopesHint: A key reaches only the endpoint groups ticked here. Identity management and cookie import always require identity:manage.

scopeHint.douyinRead: Post, author, comment and parse endpoints for Douyin.
scopeHint.identityManage: Mint, import, test and retire identities. An ordinary read key must never carry this.
scopeHint.admin: Everything, settings and users included. Grant it sparingly.

apiKeys.rateLimitHint: Requests per minute. This is abuse protection, not a billing quota: the project has no plans, metering or usage settlement. It exists so one runaway script cannot drain the identity pool. Leave empty to inherit the instance default.
apiKeys.rateLimitInvalid: Enter a whole number between {min} and {max}, or leave it empty.
apiKeys.expiryHint: An expired key stops working on its own, which limits the damage of a leak nobody noticed.
apiKeys.notBillingBody: Keys authenticate programs, scripts and agents. The console itself uses a session cookie and needs no key.
apiKeys.noteScopes: Scopes are checked on every request, even when the key belongs to an administrator.
apiKeys.notePrefix: Only the prefix is stored in clear. The secret is kept as a sha256 hash, so this page can list keys but never reveal one.
apiKeys.noteRevoke: Revocation takes effect on the next request; there is no cache to wait out.
apiKeys.revokeDescription: Calls made with {name} start failing with UNAUTHENTICATED on the next request. This cannot be undone.
apiKeys.emptyDescription: Create one per script or agent, so a single leak can be revoked without disturbing anything else.

param.url: A post or profile link, or the share text around one.
param.aweme_id: Post id. Provide this or a link.
param.sec_user_id: Stable author id. Provide this or a link.
param.comment_id: The comment whose replies you want.
param.cursor: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Leave empty for the first page.
param.include_raw: Also return the untouched platform payload.
param.wait: Seconds the server may hold the connection before answering with a task id instead.

playground.requestDescription: The console calls with your session cookie; a script would use an API key.
playground.contextDescription: Polled every few seconds, so it is current at the moment a call fails.
playground.poolEmptyHint: No identity is active. Requests are rejected with IDENTITY_POOL_EXHAUSTED until one recovers.
playground.failureDescription: The stable code, the identity that served it, the circuit and the pool, in one place.
playground.servedByPending: The request log has not caught up yet.
playground.servedByUnknown: No request id came back, so the call never reached the scheduler.
playground.normalizedDescription: The stable contract every client sees.
playground.rawDescription: The platform payload, kept because it is the evidence when a parser breaks.
playground.rawMissing: This call did not ask for the raw payload.
playground.rawEnable: Include the raw payload and run again
playground.snippetDescription: Generated from the form above. Replace the placeholder with one of your API keys.
playground.snippetNote: The console authenticates with a session cookie. Outside the browser use Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key.
playground.emptyDescription: Send a request and the normalized result and the raw platform payload appear here, side by side.

parse.inputDescription: One per line, or several separated by spaces. Share text from the app is accepted as is.
parse.inputHint: Up to {max} links per run, submitted in batches of {chunk}.
parse.tooMany: Too many links: keep it under {max}.
parse.detected: {count, plural, one {# link} other {# links}} ready · {duplicates, plural, one {# duplicate removed} other {# duplicates removed}}
parse.submit: Parse {count, plural, one {# link} other {# links}}
parse.notSubmitted: The server rejected this link before it became a task.
parse.taskGone: The task expired before its result was read.
parse.trackingNote: Submission is one request; tracking is per link, and every row can be retried on its own.
parse.emptyDescription: Paste links above and parse them. Rows appear here as each task finishes.
parse.retryNotAllowed: This error is permanent; retrying it only burns identities.
parse.downloadDescription: Files go straight from the platform CDN to your browser. The server never relays media.
parse.noVideo: No video stream in this result.
parse.downloadBlockedTitle: The browser could not fetch the file
parse.downloadBlockedBody: All {count} mirrors refused a cross-origin read, which is CORS or hotlink protection rather than a broken link. The first mirror was opened in a new tab: save it from there, or enable the optional server-side download proxy.
parse.downloadNote: A blocked download rarely means a dead file. Open the link and save it from the new tab instead.

logs.liveHint: Refreshes every few seconds. Turn it off while reading a row.
logs.filtersDescription: Every field is optional; an empty one matches everything.
logs.emptyDescription: Widen the time range, or clear a filter.
logs.auditDescription: Who changed what. Kept apart from the request log so it is never buried by ordinary traffic.
logs.auditEmptyDescription: Administrative actions appear here as they happen.

rejectReason.no_token: Every identity is out of quota
rejectReason.wait_timeout: Gave up waiting for an identity

docs.specDescription: Generated by the running instance, in the language this console is set to.
docs.assetsFailed: The Swagger UI assets could not be fetched from the CDN. On an air-gapped deployment that is expected: the raw document and the server-rendered page still work.
docs.emptyDescription: That is a deployment problem rather than an empty database: the api container registered no routes.

access.title: Endpoint access
access.description: Every endpoint needs an API key unless you open it here. Admin, authentication and setup endpoints can never be opened.
access.openWarningTitle: Open to anyone who can reach this server
access.filter: Filter by path, summary or method
access.lockedHint: Admin, authentication and setup endpoints are refused by the server whatever this page says, so they have no switch.
access.confirmTitle: Serve this endpoint without a key?
access.confirmBody: {endpoint} will answer anyone who can reach this server. Anonymous callers get read access only and are rate limited by address, but every call still spends this instance's identity pool.
access.openCount: {count, plural, =0 {No endpoint open} one {# endpoint open} other {# endpoints open}}
access.openWarning: {count, plural, one {# endpoint answers without a credential. It still costs this instance's identity pool on every call.} other {# endpoints answer without a credential. They still cost this instance's identity pool on every call.}}
